doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Favorite songwriters
summary: Asked for favorite songwriters, Mandel lists Berlin, Kern, Rodgers, Warren, Mercer and others, and mentions serving on the ASCAP board.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: I guess the only thing I haven’t asked you, is about who your favorite songwriters are and film composers are.
Okay, well how many hours have we got left?

Favorite songwriters, my God, you know the old phrase, “We stand on the shoulders of giants,” there are so many giants and I’m fortunate enough to be on the board of governors of ASCAP, I have been for the past six years and you run into these giants, or their ghosts up their because it was founded, one of the founders was Irving Berlin who was really American music basically and has been for the last you know forty, fifty years. Oh God, Berlin, Jerome Kern, Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart, I preferred the early Rodgers by far to the later Rodgers. I mean we had so many wonderful writers, Harry Warren, Johnny Mercer, Vincent Youmans, you know with everyone I name there’s probably gonna be that many I forget. Fats Waller, Duke Ellington, you can just go on and on, Cole Porter, George Gershwin I haven’t even mentioned. There’s just – you know, what a tradition we have in back of us of songwriting and I’m sure I’ve forgotten a number of giants just right now and they’re wonderful. Did I say Vincent Youmans? You know you can just go on and on.
